Description: Surrogate key; reviews and managers reference it.

Description: Outlet name as the admin typed it; the CSV outlet column must match it, ignoring case.
Why: AC-US-01-001-1: the admin adds an outlet with a name; HLD flow A matches each CSV row's outlet by this name.

Description: When the outlet was added.

Description: Last change to this row.
Why: Rule: audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Surrogate key; the only identity the JWT carries.
Why: ADR-0007: the token identifies the user only and role and outlet are re-read from this row.

Description: Sign-in name and the digest recipient address.

Description: Name shown in the top bar and beside a reply the manager marked replied.
Why: AC-US-00-003-2: the review shows as replied with the manager.

Description: The one outlet an outlet manager may see and act on; null for the brand admin.

Description: bcrypt hash from the users file; never the password.

Description: Set when the account left the users file; sign-in is refused and the row stays.
Why: AC-US-00-003-2: a replied review keeps showing its manager after that manager leaves the users file, so the row cannot be deleted.

Description: When the account was first loaded.
Why: Rule: audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Last change from the users file.
Why: Rule: audit columns; the start-up upsert changes name, role, outlet or hash.

Description: Surrogate key; reviews record the import that brought them in.
Why: HLD section 4 review fix: a review references its import so a bad import can be found.

Description: Client-made id; a repeat returns this result and imports nothing.
Why: Tenet 8: a repeated upload returns the first result with no second row.

Description: Name of the uploaded file, shown with the result.
Why: Screen S-07 success state names the imported file; a repeat must return the same result.

Description: Rows stored as new reviews; set before the import commits.
Why: AC-US-01-002-1: the admin sees how many reviews were imported.

Description: Rows skipped because the same review was already imported.
Why: HLD flow A: rows already imported are counted, not stored; S-07 shows the skipped count.

Description: Rows rejected; each is listed in import_rejections.
Why: AC-US-01-002-3 and Q-023: rejected rows are reported.

Description: When the import committed.
Why: Rule: audit columns; imports are never updated, so there is no updated_at.

Description: The import that rejected the row.
Why: AC-US-01-002-3: each rejected row is reported for its import; tenet 8 returns the same list on a repeat.

Description: Row number in the file, counted as the admin sees it in a spreadsheet.
Why: AC-US-01-002-3 and Q-023: each rejected row is reported with its row number.

Description: Why the row was rejected, worded so the admin can fix it.
Why: AC-US-01-002-3 and Q-023: each rejected row is reported with its reason.

Description: Integer id; the id the tagging batch sends and every result line must carry.
Why: AC-US-01-004-1 and tenet 4: results are stored by review id; HLD section 8 keeps ids short integers to fit 20 lines under max_tokens 1000.

Description: The outlet reviewed, matched from the CSV outlet column.
Why: REQ-003 and AC-US-01-002-2: the stored review holds its outlet; tenet 3 filters every outlet query on it.

Description: The import that brought the review in; null for reviews the seed command wrote.
Why: HLD section 4 review fix: review import; the seed (AC-US-02-006-1) writes reviews without an upload.

Description: Where the review was written, as the CSV source column says.
Why: REQ-003 and AC-US-01-002-2: the stored review holds its source unchanged.

Description: Calendar date of the review.
Why: REQ-003; Q-005 and AC-US-01-007-1: weeks run Monday to Sunday; HLD review fix: a calendar date in the brand timezone.

Description: Star rating, a whole number from 1 to 5.
Why: REQ-003; AC-US-01-005-1 averages it per week; scale 1 to 5 whole stars decided by the product owner on 2026-10-06.

Description: The review as written, kept unchanged.
Why: REQ-003 and AC-US-01-002-2; AC-US-01-008-1 searches it; it is sent to the model for tags and drafts.

Description: Name of the person who wrote the review.
Why: REQ-003 and AC-US-01-002-2; AC-US-01-008-1 searches it; required, decided by the product owner on 2026-10-06.

Description: When the review was stored.
Why: Rule: audit columns; reviews are never edited, so there is no updated_at.

Description: The review the result line named; one result per review.
Why: REQ-011 and AC-US-01-003-6: one stored result per review, never re-tagged; ADR-0006: no row means untagged.

Description: Theme codes from the configured list; zero, one or several.
Why: AC-US-01-003-2 and Q-021: zero, one or several themes from the list; AC-US-01-006-2 counts each theme once.

Description: One label: positive, neutral or negative.
Why: AC-US-01-003-4 and Q-013: one sentiment label per review.

Description: True when the review concerns food safety, harassment or a legal threat.
Why: REQ-010 and AC-US-01-003-5; AC-US-01-008-3 and AC-US-01-009-4 list urgent reviews.

Description: Number of the tagging prompt version that produced this result.
Why: AC-US-02-002-2 and Q-011: a stored tag names the prompt version that produced it.

Description: When the result was stored.
Why: Rule: audit columns; a result is never changed, so there is no updated_at.

Description: The review replied to; the primary key lets only one request claim the draft.
Why: AC-US-00-002-2: a stored draft is shown again with no model call; HLD flow B claims the row before calling the model.

Description: drafting while the model call runs, draft while editable, replied once a manager approved it.
Why: AC-US-00-003-2 and -4 and Q-008: replied only through the manager's approval; AC-US-01-008-2 filters on reply status.

Description: The text the model drafted, kept as drafted; null while drafting or when written by hand.
Why: AC-US-00-002-1: the draft is generated, stored and shown; AC-US-00-002-7: a hand-written reply has no draft.

Description: Number of the reply prompt version that drafted draft_text; null without a model draft.
Why: AC-US-00-002-3 and AC-US-02-002-2: the version is stored with the draft.

Description: The text the manager edits and approves; starts as the draft.
Why: AC-US-00-003-1: the edited text is stored and shown next time; AC-US-00-003-2: replied shows the final text.

Description: The outlet manager who marked it replied, which is the approval.
Why: AC-US-00-003-2: the review shows as replied with the manager.

Description: When the manager marked it replied.
Why: AC-US-00-003-2: the review shows as replied with the time.

Description: When the draft was claimed or the reply first written.
Why: Rule: audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Last change; a drafting claim older than 60 seconds may be taken over.
Why: Rule: audit columns; HLD section 8 draft deadline of 45 seconds, so an older drafting claim belongs to a crashed request.

Description: Surrogate key.
Why: Rule: every table has a primary key; request_id is the client's, not ours.

Description: Client-made id; a repeat returns this digest and never sends again.
Why: AC-US-01-009-5: one email; tenet 8 and HLD flow C step 3.

Description: sending before SMTP is called, then sent or failed.
Why: HLD flow C step 3: the row is claimed as sending before SMTP; HLD section 7: MailHog down marks it failed.

Description: Monday of the latest complete week the digest covers.
Why: AC-US-01-009-2 and Q-005: the latest complete Monday to Sunday week; S-08 names the week.

Description: Address the one email went to: the brand admin.
Why: AC-US-01-009-5 and Q-006: one email to the brand admin; S-08 shows who it was sent to.

Description: Reviews dated in the two compared weeks that were still untagged.
Why: HLD flow C step 2 review fix: the first line states untagged reviews in the two weeks.

Description: Email subject as sent.
Why: S-08 success state shows the email as composed; a repeat returns the recorded digest.

Description: Email body as composed, quoting urgent reviews.
Why: AC-US-01-009-3 and -4: movers and urgent reviews with their text; HLD flow C: a repeat returns the recorded digest.

Description: The SMTP error shown to the admin when sending failed.
Why: HLD section 7: MailHog down, the row is marked failed and the admin sees the error.

Description: When MailHog accepted the email.
Why: S-08 success state shows the time the digest was sent.

Description: When the digest was generated and claimed.
Why: Rule: audit columns; AC-US-01-009-1: generated at that moment.

Description: Last status change.
Why: Rule: audit columns (database postgres reference).

Description: Surrogate key; the gateway settles the row it reserved by this id.
Why: HLD section 3: a cost row is reserved before the call and settled after it.

Description: tagging, drafting, evaluation, tone_check, or reconciliation for a start-up adjustment.
Why: AC-US-02-001-1: tagging, drafting and evaluation calls all pass the gateway; AC-US-02-004-5: evaluation cost is in the total.

Description: Model identifier sent to OpenRouter; null only on a reconciliation row.
Why: AC-US-02-001-2: a log row records the model.

Description: Number of the prompt version sent; the purpose says which prompt.
Why: HLD section 10: the cost log is the audit of every call and its prompt version (Q-011).

Description: Input tokens OpenRouter reported; null until the call settles.
Why: REQ-030 and AC-US-02-001-2: a log row records input tokens.

Description: Output tokens OpenRouter reported; null until the call settles.
Why: REQ-030 and AC-US-02-001-2: a log row records output tokens.

Description: Worst-case price reserved before the call; counts until settled.

Description: usage.cost from the response, in USD; replaces the reserved price in the total.

Description: reserved while in flight, settled with a response, failed without one.
Why: HLD section 3: the running total sums settled cost, or reserved cost where not settled.

Description: When the call was reserved, which is the time the log shows.
Why: AC-US-02-001-2: a log row records the time.

Description: When the call settled or failed.
Why: Rule: audit columns (database postgres reference).
